speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These are significant symptoms; to begin my assessment, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool appearance regarding the abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of fever, night sweats, weight loss, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy (Virchow's node) raise high suspicion for malignancy, particularly lymphoma or metastatic abdominal cancer. Have you noticed any painless lumps elsewhere on your body, such as in your neck, armpits, or groin?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), abdominal pain, and a painless, fixed, supraclavicular lymph node is highly suggestive of a malignancy, specifically lymphoma or metastatic carcinoma. I will need to confirm this with imaging and a biopsy.
